rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
The heaters of Oxygen tank No. 2 ran on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours before launch. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The Apollo 13 Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in that tank. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The cause the board pointed to was the tank's thermostatic switches. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)" The board's report called the switch failure "a serious oversight in which all parties share." [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot, caught German measles about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". That exposure started the crew swap [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

The swap brought in Jack Swigert, who became Apollo 13 command module pilot in place of Ken Mattingly [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Apollo 13 role is prime command module pilot (was backup command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

Swigert was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982, but he died before taking office [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

The brain does not say how or when he died, so the cause and date of his death are not covered.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Apollo 13's 1970 dates in the brain, in order:

1. **1970-04-06: physicals and blood tests.** The blood tests showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-10: crew swap decided and announced.** A KSC management meeting replaced Mattingly with Jack Swigert, announced at a press conference. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" Swigert became command module pilot that day. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-11: launch.** [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13: oxygen tank explosion and abort.** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded about 56 hours into the flight. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" The mission goal changed from a Fra Mauro landing to a safe return. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17: splashdown.** The crew, using the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat, splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970: review board report published.** [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" The board, chaired by Edgar Cortright, traced the explosion to tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The brain gives only the month for the report, not a day.
